detail.longDescription: I have the following code: from dataclasses import dataclass @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) class Foo: attr1: int f = Foo(1) f.attr2 = 42 In Python 3.13+, I get a FrozenInstanceError , as expected: Traceback (most recent call last): File "c:\Users\1\Downloads\stackoverflow.py", line 10, in <module> f.attr2 = 42 ^^^^^^^ File "<string>", line 15, in __setattr__ dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError: cannot assign to field 'attr2' But in Python < 3.13, I get a strange TypeError : Traceback (most recent call last): File "c:\Users\1\Downloads\stackoverflow.py", line 10, in <module> f.attr2 = 42 ^^^^^^^ File "<string>", line 5, in __setattr__ TypeError: super(type, obj): obj must be an instance or subtype of type What is the reason for this behaviour? How can I work around it in Python < 3.13? E.g. how can I catch the exception raised by f.attr2 = 42 ? Note: I also tested @dataclass es using the following args with no problems: frozen=True, slots=False : this correctly raises dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError: cannot assign to field 'attr2' on both 3.12 and 3.13. frozen=False, slots=True : this correctly raises AttributeError: 'Foo' object has no attribute 'attr2' on both versions. Note: I've been here , here and here , which ask about calling super() in dataclasses. They exhibit a similar TypeError , but mine happens in __setattr__ whereas theirs is in a user-defined method.
